cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
cards.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Hide this envelope under the picnic hamper before Mum comes in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked me to unpack the hamper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Then keep the envelope in your pocket while you unpack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll end up taking it home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. I'll explain when she stops asking where it is.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 merely announce professionalism; A3 corrects no standard after B2 says Mum asked for unpacking. The secret-help Drive is clear.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 unpacking requires A3 pocket concealment and B4 taking it home leads to A5 assent, but the condescending standard phrase does not answer B2.

relationship.evidence: B2 has a real unpacking task and B4 anticipates unintended responsibility; A5 uses that concern rather than addressing consent.

heightening.evidence: A5 extends the hiding period from B4 but does not develop S03's supposed professional method.

specificity.evidence: A1 names Mum, an envelope and a hamper; its contents need not be known to understand hiding it.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 and A3 add detached professional labels to an otherwise compact five-turn concealment exchange.
